g.text: A join with no completion — the buffer and the minimum watermark
5 true matches · peak buffer 5 · 2 click never reaches its emission point
2 // Two of a row's five columns are CLOCKS, which ch01 established:
3 // et = event time, when it happened · pt = processing time, when we saw it
4 // key = which stream it is on: "a" = clicks, "b" = impressions
5 type Row { id, key, et, pt, v }
6 // primitive: EVENTS — the book's 9 rows, in ARRIVAL order (tools/stream_seed.js).
7 // EVENTS[7] = (id 7, key "b", et 50, pt 280, v 4) <- the late impression
8 // primitive: NONE — no value. Distinct from a value of 0.
9 // primitive: J — the join window, in seconds. J = 60
10 // primitive: LAG — each side's assumed worst-case skew. LAG = 60
11 // primitive: KEYS — the two sides. KEYS = ["a", "b"]
12 // primitive: LEFT / RIGHT — the side names. LEFT = "a" · RIGHT = "b"
13 // primitive: rowsOf(key) — one side of the join.
15 // primitive: absDiff(a, b) — the distance between two times. absDiff(1, 50) = 49
16 // primitive: append(xs, x) — xs with x added at the end. append([1], 2) = [1,2]
17 // primitive: indexOf(r) — r's position in ARRIVAL order. indexOf(EVENTS[7]) = 7
21 // function: trueMatches() — every pair within J. This is what the data CONTAINS,
22 // independent of what any pipeline manages to emit.
28 if (absDiff(l.et, r.et) <= J) { out = append(out, [l.id, r.id]) }
34 // function: sideWatermark(key, i) — one input's own completeness claim after row i.
40 if (seen == NONE || EVENTS[j].et > seen) { seen = EVENTS[j].et }
46 // function: joinWatermark(i) — the MINIMUM over both inputs. A silent side blocks
47 // the claim entirely, and a join always has two sides.
54 if (lowest == NONE || w < lowest) { lowest = w }
59 // function: planFor(l) — when this click may emit, and which impressions it
60 // matches. emitIdx NONE means it NEVER emits.
66 if (when == NONE && w != NONE && w > l.et + J) { when = i }
75 // function: main() — THE CALLER: all the matches, and two very different clicks.
Step 1/0 — the join predicate is one subtraction
`absDiff(1, 50)` = 49, within J = 60, so the pair is a match. 5 matches exist in this data. Note this function uses no watermark and no buffer — it is what
the data CONTAINS, which is the baseline the pipeline will be measured against.

Step 2/0 — a silent side blocks the join's claim entirely
At row 0 only the a side has produced anything, so this returns NONE — the join makes no claim at all. For a windowed aggregate one input going quiet is bad
luck; for a join it is structural, because there are always two.

Step 3/0 — one click reaches its emission point
Click 3 needs the join watermark above 130 + 60 = 190, which first happens at row 8. By then impression 2 has arrived, so it is published correctly and never
revised — 1 of the 5 clicks is in this state.

Step 4/0 — and 2 click never reaches it, holding 2 matches
Click 4 needs the watermark above 305, and `claim` only ever reaches 200. So `when` stays NONE while `ms` holds 2 real matches. They are computed, sitting in
state, and never published — and no error is raised.
